q: A contract note must be issued to the client within:
e: SEBI mandates contract note issuance within 24 hours of trade. Digital Contract Notes (DCN) are accepted. Itemises trade details + brokerage + STT + GST + DP charges.

q: STT on equity delivery transactions is:
e: Equity delivery: STT 0.1% on BOTH buy and sell sides. Intraday: 0.025% sell side only. Futures: 0.0125% sell. Options: 0.10% on premium (sell side).

q: Pre-trade margin became mandatory for all clients from:
e: SEBI mandated pre-trade margin collection starting September 2020. Brokers must collect margin upfront before placing the order. Failure = penalty.

q: GST applies on which components of a broker's transaction stack?
e: GST 18% applies on (brokerage + exchange transaction charge + SEBI turnover fee). STT and stamp duty are statutory taxes — no GST on them.

q: T+1 settlement for cash equity in India was fully implemented from:
e: Phased rollout completed in January 2023 — all NSE/BSE listed equity now settles on T+1. T+0 is optional in two windows since 2024.

q: A broker must hold client funds in:
o: The same bank account as own funds
A separate bank account designated for client funds
e: Client funds must be in a SEPARATE bank account, never co-mingled with broker's own funds. Daily 3-way reconciliation by exchange. Misuse triggers severe enforcement.

q: UCC (Unique Client Code) is mapped to:
e: UCC is PAN-mapped. One UCC per PAN per broker. Minor's UCC is linked to the guardian's PAN. All trades + funds + securities tagged to UCC.

q: An IOC (Immediate or Cancel) order:
o: Stays in the book until end of day
Executes whatever is available immediately; unmatched portion is cancelled
e: IOC orders execute as much as can be matched immediately; any unmatched portion is cancelled instantly. Partial execution allowed.

q: Order matching in India's exchanges follows:
e: Best price wins; at the same price, earliest timestamp wins. Partial fills allowed; remainder stays in the book.

q: Stamp duty on equity delivery transactions (since July 2020) is:
e: Stamp duty unified across India since July 2020: 0.015% on equity delivery (BUY side); 0.002% on F&O futures (sell); 0.003% on F&O options (sell); 0.0001% on currency.

q: DP (Depository Participant) charges are typically levied:
o: On every demat debit (sell from demat)
e: DP charges are typically ₹13-25 per scrip per debit (i.e. when securities are sold from demat). No DP charge on buys (credits) or intraday trades that don't move from demat.

q: In-Person Verification (IPV) for KYC can be done via:
o: Only physical face-to-face at the broker's office
Video call by the broker's authorised person
e: IPV can be done via video call by the broker's authorised personnel — broker-led IPV is the standard for online onboarding. Aadhaar e-KYC + IPV combination is standard.

q: Peak margin reporting is sampled at how many random points during the trading day?
e: Clearing corp samples positions at 4 random snapshots during the day. The peak margin requirement is then frozen for the day, computed for the position closed at the random snapshot.

q: PoA (Power of Attorney) for demat operations is being increasingly replaced by:
e: eDIS = electronic Demat Instruction Slip with OTP authentication per transaction. SEBI is nudging brokers from PoA (broad authority) to eDIS (transaction-specific) for client safety.

q: STT on the buyer of an exercised option is:
e: Buyer pays STT 0.125% of settlement value only when an option is exercised. Sellers pay 0.10% on premium at the time of sale, regardless of exercise.

q: A 'Group I' security in MTF eligibility refers to:
o: Highly liquid stocks meeting top-tier criteria
e: Group I = highest-liquidity stocks (impact cost low, regular trading). Only Group I stocks are MTF-eligible. T-Group, Z-Group penny stocks are excluded.

q: A discount broker typically charges brokerage of approximately:
e: Discount brokers (Zerodha, Groww, Upstox) charge ~₹20 flat per order. Full-service brokers charge 0.3-0.5% of trade value with research + advisory bundled.

q: ASBA (Application Supported by Blocked Amount) means:
o: Funds are debited only on allotment; until then they're blocked in the bank account
Funds are debited at application time
Funds are debited at IPO opening
e: ASBA blocks the IPO application amount in the investor's bank account; funds are debited only on actual allotment. The unallotted portion is unblocked back to the investor.

q: Daily client funds reconciliation by the exchange is typically:
e: Daily 3-way reconciliation: broker's books + bank statement + clearing corp records. Mismatches must be resolved same day. Mandatory under SEBI circulars.

q: Margin shortfall penalty for a first-day occurrence is approximately:
e: 0.5% per day for first occurrence, escalating for repeats. After 5 consecutive instances, the broker may need to disable client trading.

q: Two prerequisites for a person to act as a stock-broker employee handling research advice are:
e: Stock-broker employees handling client transactions / advice need relevant NISM certification + ARN (mapped through their broker firm). EUIN identifies the advising employee.

q: AP (Authorised Person) commission split with the TM is typically:
e: Typical split: 70-80% of brokerage to AP, 20-30% to TM. Exact split is per agreement. AP works at the local relationship level; TM provides infrastructure + compliance.

q: Aadhaar e-KYC for stock-broker onboarding requires:
e: Aadhaar e-KYC uses UIDAI's e-KYC service: OTP-based or biometric authentication. Allows fully digital onboarding. Combined with IPV.

q: Risk Disclosure Document (RDD) must be signed:
o: At client onboarding, before any trade
e: RDD is signed at client onboarding, BEFORE any trades. SEBI inspects this. Pre-trade RDD signing is the only compliant practice.
